_about: Who sells what at a settlement's market (docs/fix-interfaces.md §3.4, the owner's
rulings of 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-29; docs/design-d-people.md §4.8). Read by
rules/market.py. Words and lists only: every price is the Core Rulebook's, in
rules/goods.py and the weapon and armour tables, and nothing here is a number a
model could author.
SHOPS are counters with a keeper of their own. A village has the general store; a
town or city has all four. `gear` names rules/goods.py GEAR keys; `tables` names
whole Core tables (every weapon the outfit page sells goes to the weaponsmith, every
armour and shield to the armorer); `draw` names crafting benches whose priced
materials the counter draws a daily shelf from (rules/market.py `stock`).
STALLS are everything the shops do not carry, grouped 'according to their crafts'
(Colchester, 1562). `holders` is how many stallholders a market of each scale has;
the lines are dealt onto them by lot, seeded on the settlement, so a town keeps its
stalls and two towns differ. A GEAR key named nowhere lands on the `catch_all` line,
so a new catalogue row is never unsold.
STABLES sell the animals and the tack, at the prices of d20pfsrd 'Animals & Animal
Gear' (Ultimate Equipment), fetched 2026-09-29: light horse 75 gp (combat-trained
110), heavy horse 200 (300), pony 30 (45), camel 150, riding dog 150, donkey or mule
8; saddles riding 10, military 20, pack 5; bit and bridle 2; saddlebags 4; feed
5 cp a day. 'Donkeys and mules have the same statistics as ponies.' Mounts are
bought, never hired (the owner, 2026-09-29). `template` is the bestiary block the
bought animal is made from; rules/journey.py MOUNTS decides which of them can be
ridden on a journey. Where the settlement has no stables of its own, the same
counter stands at the market as the horse lines. Stabling (5 sp a night) and feed
(5 cp a mount a day) are not sold here: the engine charges them itself, feed per day
travelled or rested and stabling per night rested where there are stables
(rules/engine.py, the journey and the rest), so a counter row would charge the keep
twice.
CONSUMABLES are what a craft burns, pours or uses up in the working rather than what
the thing is made from: the forge's fuel, flux and quench, the alchemist's solvents,
salts and vials, the tanner's bark, oil, wax, thread and curing salt, the enchanter's
ink, chalk and seal. `consumables` on a shop, a stall line or a place names the crafts
whose consumables that counter ALWAYS carries, at the material's own `price_gp`,
outside the rarity quota and the daily draw (rules/market.py `consumables_at`). Which
kinds count is the `consumables` block below, by `kind` in content/materials/*.json,
never by name, so a new charcoal added to a catalogue tomorrow is on the smith's
counter tomorrow. Every kind a catalogue uses must be filed as consumed or made_from,
every common consumable must carry a `price_gp`, and every craft must be named by
some market counter: rules/market.py refuses the document otherwise, with the fix
named. Measured 2026-10-05 before this, over 60 days at a smithy counter seeded on Panthcove: charcoal
on the shelf 30 days, quenching oil 29; curing salt and oak bark at the tannery 0.
`kinds` is what is consumed by the working, per craft catalogue
(content/materials/<craft>-materials.json); `made_from` is everything else that
catalogue files, so a kind nobody has classified fails on load instead of silently
landing on no counter. The enchanter's own `consumed: true` rows (ink, chalk, salt,
catalyst, treatment) agree with its list, and the check holds them to it. `tiers` is
which rarities are staples: a common fuel is on every forge's shelf, a skymetal fire
(dwarven hearthcoal and up) stays in the daily draw where a rarity belongs. `places`
is the settlement places whose keeper sells over a counter (rules/places.py STAFFED)
and what they carry and draw; a place named nowhere keeps the general draw.
Prior art (2026-10-05): Skyrim's blacksmith chest always holds 10 iron ingots and
leather strips and its apothecary a salt pile, with only the rest drawn (UESP
Skyrim:Leveled_Lists); Stardew Valley's Clint always sells coal and ore, Pierre
always sells vinegar and oil, and randomness lives in the Traveling Cart alone;
the Core Rulebook's 75% roll is for magic items only, 'nonmagical items and gear
are generally available' (aonprd Rules ID 374).
